Pilot of the lead French dirigible that drops white phosphorus and turpentine on London.

Young Polytechnic prefect who calmly surveys the burning of London from Greenwich, conducts the demographic census of conquered Europe, and later works frantically in the Thalassia Chart-Vault during the 1919 crisis.
Lady Kaiulani's forty-year-old niece and secretary in the Insular Secretariat who reads the war-profiteering ledgers of the Neutrality Syndicate.
Syndic for the Third Rhine Canton who protests the de-industrialization and demographic conscription of Europe in the Berlin Reichstag.
Representative of the Vatican at the signing of the Geneva Accord.

legacy_profiles.legacy_name: Former Federal Councillor of the Swiss Cantons
legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Swiss representative at the signing of the Geneva Accord.
Representative of the dissolved German Quartermaster Staff at Geneva who asks only for a guarantee of the municipal salt-ration.
Captain of the dispatch-cruiser *Manila* steaming through the Strait of Messina.
Naval surgeon at the Gibraltar coal-hulks whose autopsy dispatch identifies the lethal 'Rhine-Mud Grippe'.
Administrator overseeing the soup-lines, charter-burnings, and wrist-shackling of the Austrian population in the Vienna Heldenplatz.
Last cousin of Charles the Fifth who surrenders his patent of nobility for soup and a riveted wrist-tag in Vienna.
Enlisted technician riveting permanent lead-and-brass ration-tags onto the wrists of Viennese citizens.
Sacred Emperor of the Grand Confederation; grandson of Lady Kaiulani and Elias Thorne, whose rigid insistence on mathematical infallibility and military expansion accelerates the empire's collapse.
notes: Source says grandson of Kaiulani and Elias; precise kinship remains unapproved; dead legitimate son cannot be parent
Direct Elias–Kaiulani grandparentage unproven; family line open.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Veteran supreme commander of the Combined Pacific Corps who leads the disastrous 1919 invasion of the Kingdom of Kabul and is crushed to death in the Kurd-Kabul defile.
Auditor from Thalassia killed by a ricocheting jezail slug in the Kurd-Kabul defile while carrying the November audit-rolls.
Thirty-year-old officer who reports the rout of the Bavarian debtor-company in the Khyber pass while mortally wounded.
notes: Group may contain 3+ distinct persons; do not merge as a single biographical individual

legacy_profiles.legacy_name: Brigadier / Marshal Marcus Vance the third
legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Grand-nephew of Field-Marshal Marcus Vance; incompetent, terrified technocrat who fails in Kabul, commits the Innokentyevskaya gas massacre, fails in the Mekong delta, and is finally murdered by his own mute guards in 1931.
notes: Source grand-nephew relationship to Marcus II not fully mapped
Marcus III kinship to Marcus II open.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Sixty-year-old veteran non-commissioned officer who tries to save the column in the Kurd-Kabul defile by defying young Marcus Vance's suicidal obsession with the tax-rolls.
Eighty-year-old Afghan tribesman who drops a blazing fire-pot of pine-resin and camel-dung onto Marcus Vance's treasury-van, igniting the slaughter of the baggage train.
Aged, lame military architect of the Empire and lifelong companion to Kaiulani; gives her his greatcoat at Suez and accompanies her into exile at Kalaupapa after his grand-nephew's gas massacre.
notes: Source calls him 23 in 1887 despite 1858 birth; should be around 29
Legacy 'elder' title refers to retired Marcus II; do not confuse with Marcus I.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Twenty-two-year-old King of Kings of Persia who takes Pacifica silver bribes in Tehran to guard the Mesopotamian oil flank.

legacy_profiles.legacy_name: The Warlord of the Bakhtiari (The Khan / Sardar)
legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Persian tribal cavalry leader who negotiates with the dying Kaiulani, extorting silver, carbines, and artillery in exchange for patrolling the eastern desert.

legacy_profiles.legacy_name: Junior Prefect / Senior Auditor Hoshino (the younger)
legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Devoted aide to Lady Kaiulani in Tehran who is later sent to audit the Siberian copper pits and is shot dead by mutinous French and German locomotive firemen at Mining-Sector Nine.
Commander of a forty-ton Leviathan steam-tank in the Panjshir valley whose machine is disabled and blinded by Afghan tribesmen using soapstone pits and quartz-sand.
Sixteen-year-old insurgent in the Panjshir valley who leaps onto Lieutenant Sato's tank and destroys its engine by pouring quartz-sand and sheep-dung down the blower intake.

Chief of the Chancellery and grandson of Elias Thorne's original auditor; struggles to control the rebellious Senate in 1920 and is arrested during the Great Purge of 1921 while frantically burning ledgers.
notes: Shen III later breakdown is retained but ancestor mapping pending.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Representative of the Forty-Sixth Yangtze Canton who leads the historic 1920 Senate revolt refusing Emperor Kalanimoku's ninety-million-thaler war appropriation.

legacy_profiles.legacy_name: Assessor Miller (of the Third Sacramento Canton)
legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Californian senator who joins Senator Wu in the 1920 budget revolt, protesting the loss of agricultural labor and gold reserves to the Afghan war.

Older brother of Tank-Commander Sato; witnesses the retreat from the Khyber Pass at Jamrud in 1920, rises to Junior/Senior Minister by the 1930 Centennial, and is assassinated with hydrocyanic acid in 1931.
Native officer of the Autonomous Rajput Lancers at Jamrud Fort who silently signals the end of Pacifica prestige as the Khyber rails are pulled up.
Nineteen-year-old sentry at the Krasny-Yar copper pit in Siberia who tries to quell the debtor uprising before his frozen Maxim gun jams and his tower is blown up with nitro-glycerine.
Deportee labor leader at the Krasny-Yar pit who initiates the great Siberian rebellion by having his wrist-shackle sheared off on an anvil and announcing the defeat in Kabul.
Bearded debtor-smith at Krasny-Yar who swings a ten-pound hammer to shear the Monterey rivet off the Prussian major's wrist.
Deportee locomotive fireman on the Siberian audit-train who kills the Californian cadet-engineer with a coal-pick and shoots Senior Auditor Hoshino dead.

Airship commander of the Vengeance of Oahu and later naval aide on the cruiser Monterey; reluctantly executes Marcus Vance's order to gas Innokentyevskaya, serves him at Sydney, and dies in 1931 after licking a poisoned telegraph envelope.
Commander of the Nineteenth Satsuma Provosts at Pumping-Station Six in Malaya; his skull is blown off by a Ukrainian sniper during the jungle ambush.
Nineteen-year-old officer from the Oakland sheds who takes over the Maxim gun after Takahashi's death and tries to shut the main oil pump-valve before the Belgian artilleryman ignites the gorge.
Escaped European deportee in the Malayan jungle who hurls a flaming ball of rubber-latex and coconut-husk into the ruptured Pahang oil pipeline, destroying Pumping-Station Six.
Exhausted commander of the river monitor Tonkin in the Mekong delta who explains to Marcus Vance why their ship is immobilized by rebel wire and water-hyacinths.
Twenty-year-old secret police agent checking travel-warrants and wrist-stamps in the subterranean vaults of Thalassia during the Great Purge.
Twenty-four-year-old cyborg administrator of Automated Imperial Wool-and-Ordnance Complex Number Four in Melbourne who fires steam-mortars into starving, locked-out workers.
Grey-bearded giant in a leather apron who begs Prefect Ozawa to open the manual lathes at half-ration before leading the charge against the power pylon.

One-legged former telegraph-clerk living in the ruins of San Francisco who guides the Chronicler both above ground (viewing the Sanctuary-Ark) and down into the subterranean Cathedral of the Unnumbered.
Seventy-year-old one-eyed canoe-steersman from Niihau who guides the rebel stoker Keawe through the dynamited Koloa reef to Lady Kaiulani's hut.

Charismatic mixed-race fleet-stoker who seeks Kaiulani's royal thumbprint in 1921 for a naval mutiny, and by 1930 emerges as the prophet-leader of the subterranean Cathedral of the Unnumbered in San Francisco.
notes: Keawe is an independent revolutionary, not simply foil to Kaiulani.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Gaunt, one-eyed Russian deportee who volunteers as the lead suicide-diver in the San Francisco sewer-outfall plot to blow up the New Thalassia pontoons.
Twenty-six-year-old elite naval officer and ordnance-aide to Marcus Vance who is unmasked inside the fourth suicide-diving suit in the Mission Street sewer.
notes: Hoshino surnames do not establish direct family linkage.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Pale-faced nephew of the late rebellious Australian Senator MacArthur; explains the 'frozen salamander' sabotage at Port Kembla to the Chronicler and later serves as Marcus Vance's terrified watch-officer in the Pearl Lochs bunker.

Brother of the Colonel Kalakaua killed in the Khyber Pass; commands the Fourteenth Californian and Satsuma Pacification Regiment on the Sydney quay and is dragged from his horse when his troops refuse to fire on the strikers.
notes: Group may contain 3+ distinct persons; do not merge as a single biographical individual
Different Colonel Kalakaua at Sydney? Need identify relation to original David.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Twenty-year-old Californian soldier on the right flank at Sydney Cove who initiates the mass mutiny of the Fourteenth Regiment by grounding his bayonet and ripping off his birth-cipher.
Six-foot-four mute and deaf Samoan bodyguards of Marshal Marcus Vance who secretly join Keawe's cult and crush Vance's skull inside the Third Sub-Basal Command Bunker.
Old bystander on Montgomery Street in San Francisco who warns the Chronicler to uncover his head as Julian Thorne's column passes.

Thirty-two-year-old demagogue and putative descendant of Elias Thorne who leads the populist 'Vigilance Pioneer' coup in 1931, overthrows Emperor Kalanimoku on live television, launches a disastrous expedition to Peru, and realizes in despair that his ancestor exhausted the world's frontiers.
notes: Source alleges uncertain ancestry and age 32 in 1931; approved Elias's biological son, Kaiulani's adopted son, age about 44–45
Original Julian is an alleged descendant aged 32 in 1931; approved biological son adopted by Kaiulani, born c1886–87.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Monterey Signal Corps technician who wires the neon Tele-Vision cameras in the Senate House to broadcast Kalanimoku's overthrow.
Twenty-five-year-old Insular Restoration Guard officer who leads the raid up Waimea canyon, beats Malia, burns the priest's hut, and arrests the ninety-six-year-old Lady Kaiulani.
Sixty-year-old retired hydrographer dragged out of the Monterey almshouse to navigate the transport Sierra during Julian Thorne's doomed 1932 expedition to Peru.
Red-shirted commander of the landing forces at Callao who demands rebel barricades and Inca gold, only to find starving coolies and an empty mint.
Seventy-year-old Chinese bureaucrat on the Callao seawall who informs Colonel Miller that Peru has been stripped bare for decades and has nothing left to eat but the pioneers' own mules.
First-person narrator and eighty-two-year-old Imperial Historiographer recording the final collapse of the Grand Confederation of Pacifica.
notes: Chronicler age, source reliability and earlier witnessing history need reconciliation.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Young Cantonese amanuensis and last remaining clerk of the Archive who rescues the seventy-eight folio volumes (in eight copper cylinders) and cares for the Chronicler in exile.
notes: Source's pronoun change must not automatically prove disguise
Dao's changing pronouns do not prove an invented disguise.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Forty-year-old revolutionary fleet-stoker and surviving submarine-mechanic who leads the mutiny, spares the Archive, and helps the Chronicler escape.
notes: Keawe's age and 1921 earlier actions require exact timeline.

legacy_profiles.legacy_name: Elias Thorne (The First Protector / The American Caesar)
legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Deceased founder of the First Dynasty whose seventy-ton bronze statue (*Colossus of the Meridian*) and flagship (*Elias Thorne*) are destroyed during the fall of Thalassia.
notes: Source says unmarried; approved marriage 1857 and legitimate child
Source 1852 secession scenario replaced
Memory of Elias as unmarried and without legitimate child is superseded.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Historical Japanese nobleman and naval commander who co-founded the geopolitical order with Elias Thorne fifty-eight years earlier.
notes: Old profiles span young lieutenant and high admiral; one-person continuity not proven
Takashima final legacy memory must correspond to verified timeline.

legacy_profiles.legacy_role_summary: Young mutineer accompanying Keawe who attempts to burn the Early Protectorate archives with a kerosene torch.
Revolutionary rigger atop the lead captured military traction-engine directing the toppling of Elias Thorne's statue.
Fleeing aristocrats seen fighting aboard an overturned life-raft in the burning Pearl Lochs.
